subject: chemistry
question_text: Calculate the kinetic energy of 5 moles of nitrogen at 27 °C.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. ARITHMETIC: the book answers 4500 cal using R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, a rounding of 1.987. This card works in SI (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ → 1.87 × 10⁴ J) and shows the book's calorie form beside it; the two agree within the rounding of R. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Arithmetic re-verified: 1.5 × 5 × 8.314 × 300 = 18 706.5 J ≈ 1.87 × 10⁴ J, and the calorie form 1.5 × 5 × 2 × 300 = 4500 cal — both printed values correct. Added one clause to the first step's why saying (3/2)nRT is the TRANSLATIONAL kinetic energy, so a student who knows N₂ is diatomic is not told the card is wrong. No marked line changed. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round): the calorie line called 4500 cal the same energy in calories, but 18 706.5 J is 4471 cal; the two figures agree only under the rounded R = 2, so the bracket now says that instead of claiming an exact equality. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round 3): the step-2 margin note told the student to box the SI value while the why and the insider note said the book's printed answer is the calorie figure — advice against the printed key, and the two KE cards worded it differently. Both cards now say the same thing: the book prints the calorie value, and the student boxes whichever value they actually calculated. OPEN FOR THE TEACHER GATE: whether a Telangana IPE examiner wants the calorie figure the book prints or the SI value in the box.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula and substitution
steps.why: The kinetic energy of n moles of any gas depends only on n and the absolute temperature: KE = (3/2)nRT. (This is the translational kinetic energy the kinetic gas equation gives; a molecule is treated as a moving point, so the same (3/2)nRT is used for diatomic N₂.) The Celsius temperature must become kelvin before substitution.
common_mistakes: Substituting T = 27 instead of 300 K. The conversion to kelvin is where this mark is usually lost.
steps.memory_tip: Three halves n R T. Convert to kelvin first, substitute second.
steps.margin_note: The formula with T = 300 K on its own line earns this mark before any arithmetic.

steps.label: The answer with its unit
lines: With R ≈ 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹: KE = (3/2) × 5 × 2 × 300
= 4500 cal (using the rounded R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
steps.why: Multiplying out: 5 × 8.314 = 41.57; times 300 gives 12 471; times 1.5 gives 18 706.5 J. The book prints its answer in calories, 4500 cal, using the rounded R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; the SI line is the same formula with R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, and the two agree to the rounding of R.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer without a unit. J (or cal) is part of this mark.
Mixing units: R in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ gives joules, R in cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ gives calories. Pick one and say which.
steps.memory_tip: One mole near room temperature carries about 3.7 kJ; five moles carry about five times that, near 19 kJ.
steps.margin_note: The book's printed answer is the calorie figure, 4500 cal. Write both lines and box the value you actually calculated: the SI value if you used R = 8.314, the calorie value if you used R = 2.

insider_note: The book prints this answer in calories: 4500 cal, using R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. The SI value 1.87 × 10⁴ J is the same formula with R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, and the two agree to the rounding of R. Write both lines, box the one you calculated, and never mix the two R values in one calculation. The same question is also set with n = 2 — the paper-setters reuse the template, so read n carefully on the day.
